summary: William Lyon's talk introduces the 'knowledge graph mullet' analogy—property graph in the front, RDF triples in the back—to advocate combining two traditionally separate graph paradigms for a hybrid, versatile approach to knowledge graphs. Property graphs use nodes, relationships with types and direction, and key-value pair properties, queried via pattern matching (often Cypher). RDF, from the semantic web world, uses subject-predicate-object triples and ontologies, queried via SPARQL. Dgraph, open-sourced in 2017 by former Google engineers inspired by Spanner Graph, is presented as a hybrid: it uses the property graph model for data modeling and querying, but stores data as RDF triples with unique node IDs mapping to disk offsets for efficient traversal. A key optimization is the posting list, which groups by predicate and stores lists of connected node IDs. DQL, Dgraph's query language inspired by GraphQL, uses root criteria to find starting nodes, nested selection sets for traversal, and returns JSON matching the query structure. A news article knowledge graph example demonstrates GraphRAG using multiple subgraph entry points—vector similarity search, geospatial indices, and image embeddings—then traversing the domain graph to find richer context beyond naive RAG. Hands-on demonstrations using Ratel show DQL queries for article counts, topic traversal, date filtering with geographic traversal, 50km proximity search around NYC, and vector similarity search for 'money laundering' articles followed by topic-based traversal. Lyon then introduces the Dgraph MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, which exposes database tools to AI models for query execution, schema inspection, and mutations. Use cases include agentic coding assistants (Windsurf, Cursor) for autogenerating CRUD endpoints and exploratory data analysis in Claude Desktop, demonstrated by creating fictitious e-commerce data, generating graph visualizations, and building product recommendation queries. He presents Modus, an open-source agent orchestration framework using WebAssembly to support multiple language SDKs (Go, AssemblyScript) with a unified GraphQL API and sandboxed runtime for stateful, long-running agents. Finally, he demonstrates Hypermode Agents for creating domain-specific agents from a prompt with MCP-powered connections to GitHub, Notion, and company docs, showing a social media intern agent that analyzes a GitHub repo, generates posts with code snippets, saves to Notion, and can be ejected to Modus code for further customization. Hypermode Agents is in early access.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: The Knowledge Graph Mullet Analogy
sections.summary: Lyon introduces the mullet haircut analogy—business in the front, party in the back—extended to knowledge graphs as property graph in the front, RDF triples in the back, combining benefits of both paradigms for a versatile, low-maintenance approach.

sections.title: Property Graph vs RDF Paradigms
sections.summary: Contrasts property graphs (nodes, relationships, key-value properties, pattern matching, Cypher) with RDF (triples, ontologies, SPARQL, semantic web origins) and introduces the working definition of a knowledge graph as an instance of a property graph with canonical entity representations ('things, not strings').

sections.title: Dgraph Overview and Hybrid Architecture
sections.summary: Dgraph, open-sourced in 2017 by former Google engineers inspired by Spanner Graph, uses property graph model for data modeling and querying but RDF triples for storage. Explains how unique node IDs map to disk offsets and how the posting list optimization groups by predicate for efficient traversal.

sections.title: DQL Query Language
sections.summary: DQL, inspired by GraphQL, uses root criteria (often via index) to find starting nodes, nested selection sets for traversal specification, and returns JSON matching the query structure. Every DQL traversal starts with a well-defined starting point.

sections.title: News Knowledge Graph Model
sections.summary: Demonstrates building a knowledge graph from New York Times articles: article nodes with URL, publish date, title, abstract; connected to author, topics, organizations, geographic areas, images, and paragraph chunks with embedding properties for vector search entry points.

sections.title: GraphRAG Approach and Entry Points
sections.summary: GraphRAG uses multiple subgraph entry points—vector similarity search (lexical graph), geospatial indices, image embeddings—then traverses the domain graph to find enriched context. Unlike naive RAG which stops at vector search, GraphRAG traverses through topics and relationships to find additional relevant articles.

sections.title: Hands-on DQL Demonstrations with Ratel
sections.summary: Live demonstrations using Ratel query workbench: simple article count, topic traversal, date-filtered geographic traversal, 50km proximity search around NYC, vector similarity search for 'money laundering' articles, and complex traversal through topic nodes to find overlapping articles.

sections.title: Dgraph MCP Server Overview
sections.summary: Announces that all Dgraph enterprise features are now in a single open-source release, and introduces the MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for Dgraph as a way to expose database tools to AI models.

sections.title: Dgraph MCP Server Use Cases and Claude Desktop Demo
sections.summary: MCP server exposes readonly (queries, schema inspection) and full (mutations, schema alteration) endpoints. Use cases include agentic coding assistants (Windsurf, Cursor) for autogenerating CRUD endpoints and exploratory data analysis in Claude Desktop. Demo shows Claude creating fictitious e-commerce data (customers, products, orders), generating schema and mutations, verifying data, creating graph visualizations, and generating product recommendation queries using collaborative filtering, content-based, and demographic approaches.

sections.title: Modus Agent Orchestration Framework
sections.summary: Introduces Modus, an open-source agent orchestration framework for creating stateful, long-running AI agents. Uses WebAssembly to target multiple languages (Go, AssemblyScript), generating a unified GraphQL API from defined types and function signatures. Provides a sandboxed runtime for security, with WebAssembly details abstracted from the user.

sections.title: Hypermode Agents Demo and Conclusion
sections.summary: Demonstrates Hypermode Agents for building domain-specific agents from a prompt with MCP-powered connections. A social media intern agent is created with access to GitHub, Notion, and company docs, then tasked with analyzing the hyper-news GitHub repo to generate social media posts with code snippets and save them to Notion. The 'eject to code' feature converts the agent to Modus code for further customization. Hypermode Agents is in early access. Lyon concludes with a recap of the knowledge graph mullet for building GraphRAG workflows as the foundation for AI agents.

Filtering articles by publish date then traversing to geographic areas mentioned

Vector similarity search using embedding of 'money laundering' to find related articles, then traversing to topics, regions, organizations
Complex traversal from vector-matched articles through topic nodes to find other articles with overlapping topics not caught by vector search
Claude Desktop with Dgraph MCP server: creating fictitious e-commerce customer/product/order data by generating schema and mutations
Claude generating graph visualization JavaScript and DQL queries for the e-commerce graph
Product recommendation queries using collaborative filtering, content-based, and demographic approaches combined into a single DQL query

limitations: Mullet analogy is acknowledged as needing patience from the audience
Chunking approach in the news example is simplified—every paragraph is a chunk rather than using semantic structure
Claude does not always generate correct DQL queries on the first attempt and must iterate to get expected results
